cards.existing: Useful gender check: `ei` (his) triggers soft mutation, `ei` (her) triggers aspirate. `Ei gath` (his cat – soft) vs `ei chath` (her cat – aspirate).

cards.target: Doedd e ddim yn gwybod yr ateb i'r cwestiwn.

cards.existing: Welsh has two `you` forms: `ti` (informal singular) and `chi` (formal singular and plural). Different verb forms: `wyt ti'n` (informal) vs `ydych chi'n` (formal/plural).

cards.target: Dylen nhw wrando'n ofalus.

cards.target: Coginioch chi swper blasus.

cards.existing: Welsh is less strict about formality than German or Russian. Many speakers default to `chi` with adults they don't know, but `ti` spreads quickly once you're on first-name terms.

cards.existing: Past obligation: `Roedd rhaid i mi fynd` (I had to go). Future: `Bydd rhaid i mi fynd` (I'll have to go). The `rhaid` part stays put; the auxiliary marks tense.
